# @adexdsamson/forge — Full LLM Reference

Forge is a cross-platform React form library that wraps react-hook-form with a composable API. Call `useForge()` to get the full RHF toolkit plus an augmented `control`, render `<Forge control={...}>` as the form container, and drop `<Forger>` field wrappers around any custom input — web or React Native. Platform detection is automatic: web renders a real `<form>`, React Native renders a Fragment. All form state lives in react-hook-form's `Control` object — Forge is a thin orchestration layer, not a separate state store.

---

## What Forge Is

Forge is a cross-platform React form library that wraps [react-hook-form](https://react-hook-form.com/) with a streamlined, composable API. The mental model is three pieces: call `useForge()` to get the full react-hook-form toolkit plus an augmented `control`, render `<Forge control={...}>` as the form container, and drop `<Forger>` field wrappers around any custom input — web or React Native. Platform detection is automatic: on web, `<Forge>` renders a real `<form>` element; on React Native it renders a Fragment. All form state lives in react-hook-form's `Control` object — Forge is a thin orchestration layer, not a separate state store.

## The 8 Exports

| Export | Type | One-line purpose |
|--------|------|-----------------|
| `useForge` | Hook | Initializes form; returns full RHF toolkit + augmented `control` |
| `Forge` | Component | Form container; web=`<form>`, RN=Fragment; wires submit + wizard |
| `Forger` | Component | Connects one field to RHF via `useController`; auto event handlers |
| `useFieldArray` | Hook | Dynamic field arrays with per-item `inputProps` preservation |
| `useForgeValues` | Hook | Thin `setValue`/`getValue`/`getValues` wrapper over RHF public API |
| `usePersist` | Hook | Autosave/draft: fires handler on every value change + state flags |
| `useSubscribe` | Hook | Subscribe to any RHF `Subject<T>`; cleans up on unmount |
| `validateField` | Function | Async field validator; platform-aware (web + RN) |

Additional exports — types (`ForgeControl`, `ForgeProps`, `ForgerProps`, `UseForgeProps`, `UseForgeResult`, `FieldProps`, `ForgeSubmitButtonProps`, `FormPropsRef`, etc.), React Native helpers (`REACT_NATIVE_COMPONENTS`, `getEventHandlerName`, `getValuePropertyName`, `setReactNativeError`, `mergePlatformProps`, etc.), and platform detection booleans (`isWeb`, `isReactNative`, `isMobile`) — see [docs/API.md](docs/API.md) for the full surface.

## Recipes

### a. Basic web form

```tsx
import { useForge, Forge, Forger } from '@adexdsamson/forge';

function SignupForm() {
  const { control, formState } = useForge({
    defaultValues: { email: '', password: '' },
  });

  const onSubmit = (data: { email: string; password: string }) => {
    console.log(data);
  };

  return (
    <Forge control={control} onSubmit={onSubmit}>
      <Forger name="email" component={TextInput} rules={{ required: 'Email is required' }} />
      <Forger name="password" component={PasswordInput} rules={{ minLength: { value: 8, message: 'Too short' } }} />
      <button type="submit">Sign Up</button>
    </Forge>
  );
}
```

### b. React Native form

Pass native props (e.g. `keyboardType`, `secureTextEntry`) **directly** on `<Forger>`. Use `forgeSubmit` on buttons — Forge injects `onPress` automatically.

```tsx
import { useForge, Forge, Forger } from '@adexdsamson/forge';

function LoginForm() {
  const { control } = useForge({
    defaultValues: { email: '', password: '' },
  });

  return (
    <Forge control={control} platform="react-native" onSubmit={(data) => console.log(data)}>
      <Forger name="email" component={TextInput} keyboardType="email-address" autoCapitalize="none" />
      <Forger name="password" component={TextInput} secureTextEntry />
      <TouchableOpacity forgeSubmit>
        <Text>Log In</Text>
      </TouchableOpacity>
    </Forge>
  );
}
```

### c. Dynamic field array

```tsx
import { useForge, Forge, Forger, useFieldArray } from '@adexdsamson/forge';

function PhoneList() {
  const { control } = useForge({ defaultValues: { phones: [{ number: '' }] } });
  const { fields, append, remove } = useFieldArray({
    control,
    name: 'phones',
    inputProps: { placeholder: 'Phone number' },
  });

  return (
    <Forge control={control} onSubmit={(d) => console.log(d)}>
      {fields.map((field, i) => (
        <div key={field.id}>
          <Forger name={`phones.${i}.number`} component={TextInput} {...field.inputProps} />
          <button type="button" onClick={() => remove(i)}>Remove</button>
        </div>
      ))}
      <button type="button" onClick={() => append({ number: '' })}>Add phone</button>
      <button type="submit">Save</button>
    </Forge>
  );
}
```

### d. Autosave / persist

The handler fires on every value change and once on mount. Gate on `isDirty` to skip the initial emission if needed.

```tsx
import { useForge, Forge, Forger, usePersist } from '@adexdsamson/forge';

function AutosaveForm() {
  const { control } = useForge({ defaultValues: { notes: '' } });

  usePersist({
    control,
    handler: (values, { isDirty, isValid }) => {
      if (isDirty) saveToServer(values);
    },
  });

  return (
    <Forge control={control}>
      <Forger name="notes" component={TextArea} />
    </Forge>
  );
}
```

### e. Wizard multi-step

```tsx
import { useForge, Forge, Forger } from '@adexdsamson/forge';

function WizardForm() {
  const { control } = useForge({
    defaultValues: { name: '', email: '', plan: '' },
    isWizard: true,
    totalSteps: 2,
  });

  return (
    <Forge control={control} onSubmit={(d) => console.log(d)}>
      {/* Step 0 */}
      <div>
        <Forger name="name" component={TextInput} />
        <Forger name="email" component={TextInput} />
        <button type="button" data-wizard-nav="next">Next</button>
      </div>
      {/* Step 1 */}
      <div>
        <Forger name="plan" component={PlanPicker} />
        <button type="button" data-wizard-nav="previous">Back</button>
        <button type="button" data-wizard-nav="next">Submit</button>
      </div>
    </Forge>
  );
}
```

### f. Transform

`output` transforms the value **before writing to RHF** (display → stored). `input` transforms the value **before passing to the component** (stored → display).

```tsx
<Forger
  name="price"
  component={CurrencyInput}
  transform={{
    output: (v) => parseFloat(String(v).replace(/[^0-9.]/g, '')),
    input: (v) => `$${Number(v).toFixed(2)}`,
  }}
/>
```

### g. Schema resolver (Zod)

```tsx
import { zodResolver } from '@hookform/resolvers/zod';
import { z } from 'zod';

const schema = z.object({ email: z.string().email(), age: z.number().min(18) });

const { control } = useForge({
  resolver: zodResolver(schema),
  defaultValues: { email: '', age: 0 },
});
// No `rules` prop needed on <Forger> — the resolver handles all validation
```

### h. Standalone validateField

```tsx
import validateField from '@adexdsamson/forge';

const errors = await validateField(
  field,           // RHF Field object
  formValues,      // current form values
  false,           // validateAllFieldCriteria
);
```

## Common Mistakes

1. **do NOT** pass RN native props via a `reactNative={{}}` prop: `<Forger reactNative={{ keyboardType: 'email-pad' }}>` → **do** pass them directly: `<Forger keyboardType="email-pad">`. `ForgerController` spreads `...rest` directly onto the component; there is no `reactNative` key — it would be silently ignored.

2. **do NOT** omit the `name` prop: `<Forger component={MyInput}>` → **do** always include it: `<Forger name="email" component={MyInput}>`. `isInputSlot` checks `child.props.name`; nameless inputs are not wired into the form.

3. **do NOT** hand-wire `onPress={handleSubmit(onSubmit)}` on RN buttons inside `<Forge>`: `<TouchableOpacity onPress={handleSubmit(onSubmit)}>` → **do** use `<TouchableOpacity forgeSubmit>`. Forge injects `onPress` automatically and strips the `forgeSubmit` prop before it reaches the host component. Web: a `<button type="submit">` inside `<Forge>` just works — no manual handler needed.

4. **do NOT** assume `<Forge platform="react-native">` renders a `<View>` or any container element → **do** wrap in your own `<View>` for layout. Forge renders a React Fragment on React Native; there is no wrapper element, and `className` has no effect.

5. **do NOT** confuse transform directions — `output` transforms the display value, `input` transforms the stored value → **do** remember: `output` transforms value **before writing to RHF** (display→stored); `input` transforms value **before passing to the component** (stored→display).

6. **do NOT** render `<Forger>` outside `<Forge>` without a `control` prop: `<Forger name="x" component={Input}>` (no FormProvider context, no `control` prop) → **do** pass `control` explicitly: `<Forger name="x" component={Input} control={control}>`. Forger falls back to the `control` prop when there is no FormProvider context.

7. **do** expect `usePersist` handler to fire once on mount (drain the initial emission; gate on `isDirty` if needed). **do NOT** call `getValue("nonexistentField")` from `useForgeValues` — it throws a named Forge error (`useForgeValues.getValue: field "..." is not registered`) on fields absent from `getValues()`.

## TypeScript Quick Reference

| Type | Source | Notes |
|------|--------|-------|
| `ForgeControl<T>` | `@adexdsamson/forge` | RHF `Control<T>` augmented with Forge metadata |
| `ForgeProps<T>` | `@adexdsamson/forge` | Props for `<Forge>`; `control` is required |
| `ForgerProps<T>` | `@adexdsamson/forge` | Props for `<Forger>`; extra props spread to `component` |
| `UseForgeProps` | `@adexdsamson/forge` | Options for `useForge`; mirrors RHF `useForm` options + wizard config |
| `UseForgeResult<T>` | `@adexdsamson/forge` | Return type of `useForge`; `control` is `ForgeControl<T>` |
| `FieldProps` | `@adexdsamson/forge` | Shape for declarative `fields` array passed to `useForge` |
| `FormPropsRef` | `@adexdsamson/forge` | Ref shape for programmatic `onSubmit()` via `<Forge ref={...}>` |
| `ForgeSubmitButtonProps` | `@adexdsamson/forge` | Add `forgeSubmit` to any RN button to auto-wire `onPress` |

## Condensed API Signature Table

| Export | Signature | Notes |
|--------|-----------|-------|
| `useForge<T>` | `(props: UseForgeProps) => UseForgeResult<T>` | Props: defaultValues, resolver, fields, mode, isWizard, initialStep, totalSteps |
| `Forge<T>` | `(props: ForgeProps<T>) => JSX.Element` | Props: control (required), onSubmit, className, noValidate, children, ref, debug, platform, isWizard |
| `Forger<T>` | `(props: ForgerProps<T>) => JSX.Element` | Props: name (required), component (required), rules, transform, handler, label, control; extra props spread to component via ...rest |
| `useFieldArray<IP,T>` | `(props: ForgeFieldArray<T,...> & { inputProps: IP }) => UseFieldArrayReturn & { fields: (RHFField & { inputProps: IP })[] }` | Wraps RHF useFieldArray; adds per-item inputProps |
| `useForgeValues<T>` | `({ control }) => { setValue, getValue, getValues }` | getValue throws on unknown field |
| `usePersist<T>` | `({ control, handler }) => void` | handler: (values: T, { isDirty, isValid }) => void; fires on mount |
| `useSubscribe<T>` | `({ subject, next, disabled? }) => void` | Generic Subject<T> observer; cleans up on unmount |
| `validateField` | `(field: Field, formValues, validateAllFieldCriteria, ...) => Promise<InternalFieldErrors>` | Platform-aware; web uses reportValidity; RN uses setNativeProps |
